description: Ginger (Hassan) extracted facts. Each case: excerpt must occur on the cited page; each claim field value must occur in the excerpt.

cases.claim: Karnataka is one of seven states that together contribute 65 percent of India's ginger production.
cases.expectedExcerpt: states namely Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Orissa, Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat together contribute 65 percent to the country's total production.

cases.claim: Ginger is cultivated from sea level up to 1500 m altitude, under rainfed or irrigated conditions.
cases.expectedExcerpt: cultivated from sea level to an altitude of 1500 m above sea level. Ginger can be grown both under rain-fed and irrigated conditions.

cases.claim: Moderate rain at sowing until sprouting, heavy well-distributed showers in the growing period, and about a month of dry weather before harvest are necessary.

fields.preHarvest: dry weather for about a month

cases.expectedExcerpt: a moderate rainfall during sowing time till the rhizomes sprout, fairly heavy and well distributed showers during the growing period and dry weather for about a month before harvesting are necessary.

cases.claim: Ginger thrives best in well-drained sandy loam, clay loam, red loam or lateritic loam; friable humus-rich loam is ideal.

fields.textures: sandy loam, clay loam, red loam or lateritic loam

cases.expectedExcerpt: Ginger thrives best in well drained soils like sandy loam, clay loam, red loam or lateritic loam. A friable loam rich in humus is ideal.

cases.claim: IISR Varada: fresh mean yield 22.6 t/ha, maturity 200 days, dry recovery 20.7% (variety release data, not a regional yield).
cases.notes: Column order (yield, maturity, dry recovery, crude fibre, oleoresin, essential oil) taken from the table header on the same page.

cases.claim: IISR Surasa (vegetable purpose): fresh mean yield 24.33 t/ha, maturity 210-240 days, dry recovery 21.97%.
cases.expectedExcerpt: IISR Surasa 24.33 210-240 21.97 5.5 4.45 1.66 Plumpy bold rhizomes suitable for vegetable purpose

cases.claim: On the West Coast of India the best planting time is the first fortnight of May with pre-monsoon showers.
cases.expectedExcerpt: The best time for planting ginger in the West Coast of India is during the first fortnight of May with the receipt of pre -monsoon showers.
cases.notes: Scope is the West Coast of India, not Karnataka state or Hassan district.

cases.claim: Irrigated ginger can be planted from mid-February or early March.

fields.window: middle of February or early March

cases.expectedExcerpt: Under irrigated conditions, it can be planted well in advance during the middle of February or early March.
cases.notes: Follows the West Coast sentence in the same paragraph; regional scope is inherited, not restated.

cases.claim: Seed rhizome pieces are 2.5-5.0 cm long, 20-25 g, with one or two buds.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Carefully preserved seed rhizomes are cut into pieces of 2.5-5.0 cm length weighing 20 -25 g each having one or two good buds.
cases.notes: Canonical Unit enum has no cm or g; values kept in sourceUnits only.

cases.claim: Seed rate is 1500-1800 kg/ha in Kerala and 2000-2500 kg/ha at higher altitudes.
cases.expectedExcerpt: In Kerala, the seed rate varies from 1500 to 1800 kg ha-1. At higher altitudes the seed rate may vary from 2000 to 2500 kg ha-1.
cases.notes: First value is Kerala-specific; the guide gives no Karnataka seed rate. 'Higher altitudes' is not tied to a state.

cases.claim: Spacing between rows is 20-25 cm (the along-row spacing is stated on page 10, not on this page).
cases.expectedExcerpt: along the rows and 20-25 cm between the rows.
cases.notes: Sentence begins on page 10 ('planted at a spacing of 20-25 cm') and continues on page 11; only the page-11 part is quoted.

cases.claim: IISR Table 3 lists a Karnataka blanket schedule of FYM/compost 25 t/ha and NPK 100:50:50 kg/ha.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Karnataka FYM/compost 25 t ha-1; NPK 100:50:50 kg ha-1.
cases.notes: Recorded as evidence of state-specific scope only. Not used for any task amount: PRD 9.2 gates numeric nutrient advice on soil/management data.

cases.claim: Mulching beds with green leaves or organic wastes is essential against soil splash and erosion from heavy rain.

fields.practice: Mulching the beds with green leaves/organic wastes is essential

cases.expectedExcerpt: Mulching the beds with green leaves/organic wastes is essential to prevent soil splashing and erosion of soil due to heavy rain.

cases.claim: Green-leaf mulch is repeated at 7.5 t/ha at 45 and 90 days after planting.
cases.expectedExcerpt: repeated @ 7.5 tonnes ha-1 at 45 and 90 days after planting, immediately after weeding, application of fertilizers and earthing up.

cases.claim: Rainfed ginger is grown in high-rainfall areas with uniform rain for 5-7 months; elsewhere it is irrigated.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Ginger is cultivated as rainfed crop in high rainfall areas (uniform distribution for 5 to 7 months) and irrigated crop in less rainfall areas where distribution is not uniform.

cases.claim: Ginger needs 1300-1500 mm of water over the crop cycle.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Ginger requires 1300 -1500 mm of water during its crop cycle.

cases.claim: Critical irrigation stages: germination, rhizome initiation at 90 DAP, rhizome development at 135 DAP.
cases.expectedExcerpt: for irrigation are during germination, rhizome initiation (90 DAP) and rhizome development stages (135 DAP).

cases.claim: Irrigate right after planting, then every 7-10 days under conventional irrigation depending on weather and soil.
cases.expectedExcerpt: The first irrigation should be done immediately after planting and subsequent irrigations are given at intervals of 7 to 10 days in conventional irrigation (based on prevailing weather and soil type).

cases.claim: Provide drainage channels to avoid water stagnation.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Proper drainage channels are to be provided to avoid stagnation of water.

cases.claim: In Karnataka ginger is mixed with ragi, red gram and castor and intercropped in coconut, arecanut, coffee and orange plantations.
cases.expectedExcerpt: In Karnataka, ginger is also mix cropped with ragi, red gram and castor. Ginger is also grown as an intercrop in coconut, arecanut, coffee and orange plantations in Kerala and Karnataka.

cases.claim: Avoid rotation with tomato, potato, chillies, brinjal and peanut (hosts of Ralstonia solanacearum).

fields.avoid: tomato, potato, chillies, brinjal and peanut

cases.expectedExcerpt: crop rotation using tomato, potato, chillies, brinjal and peanut should be avoided, as these plants are hosts for the wilt causing organism, Ralstonia solanacearum.

cases.claim: Soft rot is the most destructive ginger disease and causes total loss of affected clumps.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Soft rot is the most destructive disease of ginger which results in total loss of affected clumps.

cases.claim: Soft-rot pathogen builds up with soil moisture at south-west monsoon onset; young sprouts are most susceptible.
cases.expectedExcerpt: The fungus multiplies with build up of soil moisture with the onset of south west monsoon. Younger sprouts are most susceptible to the pathogen.

cases.claim: Soft-rot inspection cue: light yellowing of lower-leaf margins spreading to the lamina.

fields.symptom: light yellowing of the leaf margins of lower leaves

cases.expectedExcerpt: Foliar symptoms appear as light yellowing of the leaf margins of lower leaves which gradually spreads to the leaf lamina.

cases.claim: Choosing well-drained soil matters because water stagnation predisposes ginger to soft-rot infection.

fields.risk: stagnation of water predisposes the plant to infection

cases.expectedExcerpt: selection of well drained soils for planting is important, since stagnation of water predisposes the plant to infection.

cases.claim: Bacterial-wilt inspection cue: mild drooping and curling of lower-leaf margins spreading upwards.

fields.symptom: mild drooping and curling of leaf margins of the lower leaves

cases.expectedExcerpt: The first conspicuous symptom is mild drooping and curling of leaf margins of the lower leaves which spread upwards.

cases.claim: Shoot-borer inspection cue: bore-hole with frass on the pseudostem and a withered yellow central shoot.
cases.expectedExcerpt: The presence of a bore -hole on the pseudostem through which frass is extruded and the withered and yellow central shoot is a characteristic symptom of pest infestation.

cases.claim: Full maturity is 210-240 days after planting; vegetable-purpose harvest starts after 180 days depending on demand.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Ginger attains full maturity in 210 -240 days after planting. Harvesting of ginger for vegetable purpose starts after 180 days based on the demand.
cases.notes: The source does not state '8-9 months'; it states 210-240 days.

cases.claim: For dry ginger, harvest at full maturity, when leaves turn yellow and start drying.

fields.indicator: leaves turn yellow and start drying

cases.expectedExcerpt: for making dry ginger, the matured rhizomes are harvested at full maturity i.e. when the leaves turn yellow and start drying.
cases.notes: Indicator is stated for dry-ginger harvest at full maturity.

cases.claim: Stop irrigation one month before harvest.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Irrigation is stopped one month before harvest and the rhizome clumps are lifted carefully with a spade or digging fork.

cases.claim: Harvest can be delayed for some months without deterioration (duration not quantified).
cases.expectedExcerpt: Late harvest is also practiced, as the crop does not deteriorate by leaving it for some months underground.

cases.claim: Vegetable-purpose harvest stage: 5-6 months after planting.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Vegetable purpose and preparation of ginger preserve, candy, soft drinks, pickles and alcoholic beverages 5-6
cases.notes: 5-6 months (about 150-183 days) is earlier than the prose 'after 180 days' on the same page; both are recorded.

cases.claim: Dried-ginger harvest stage: 7-8 months after planting.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Dried ginger and preparation of ginger oil, oleoresin, dehydrated and bleached ginger 7-8

cases.claim: Dry ginger yield is about 19-25 percent of fresh weight, varying by variety and climatic zone.
cases.expectedExcerpt: The yield of dry ginger is about 19 -25 per cent of fresh ginger depending on the variety and climatic zone.

cases.claim: The guide states its chemical formulations may not be on the CIBRC list of approved pesticides for ginger.

fields.approval: may not be included in the list of approved pesticides

cases.expectedExcerpt: The formulations may not be included in the list of approved pesticides for ginger by CIBRC.

cases.claim: The plan covers Hassan district, Karnataka.
cases.expectedExcerpt: State: KARNATAKA Agriculture Contingency Plan for District: HASSAN

cases.claim: District reference point altitude is 943 m.
cases.notes: One district reference point; farm elevation varies (Open-Meteo grid cell 954 m).

cases.claim: Kharif (June-Sep) normal rainfall 604.9 mm over 40 rainy days; normal onset 1st-2nd week of June, cessation 2nd week of September.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Kharif (June-Sep): 604.9 40 1 st to 2nd Week of June 2 nd Week of Sept

cases.claim: Summer (Apr-May) normal rainfall 168.7 mm over 12 rainy days.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Summer (Apr-May) 168.7 12

cases.claim: Annual normal rainfall 1031.2 mm over 65 rainy days (district normal).
cases.expectedExcerpt: Annual 1031.2 65
cases.notes: District normal; intra-district variation is not given in this document.

cases.claim: 80.8 thousand ha (12.2%) of Hassan has deep red soils with moderate/poor drainage in the plains.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Deep Red soils with Moderate/ poor drained soils in plains . 80.8 12.2 %

cases.claim: Net irrigated area 88.6 thousand ha versus rainfed area 255.0 thousand ha (district totals, all crops).
cases.expectedExcerpt: Irrigation Area ('000 ha) Net irrigated area 88.6 Gross irrigated area 97.4 Rainfed area 255.0

cases.claim: The horticulture crop table (continuing on page 7) reports area in thousand hectares.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Major Horticulture Crops cultivated Area ('000 ha) Total area Fruits

cases.claim: Ginger is the largest spice by area in Hassan: 13.8 (thousand ha per the page-6 header).
cases.expectedExcerpt: Spices Total Area Ginger 13.8 Cardamom 7.5 Pepper 2.7 Turmeric 0.1
cases.notes: Unit header is on page 6. Data year is not stated for this table. Plausibility of 13.8 thousand ha is not independently verified (DATA_AUDIT open item).

cases.claim: The district sowing-window table covers paddy, ragi, maize, potato and sunflower only; it gives no ginger window.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Sowing window for 5 major field crops (start and end of normal sowing week) Paddy Ragi Maize Potato Sunflower

cases.claim: Drought is a contingency the district is prone to; 2003 received 53% of normal rain.
cases.expectedExcerpt: Drought √ In 2003 (53 % of Normal Rains)
cases.notes: Whether the tick is in the 'Regular' or 'Occasional' column is lost in text extraction.

cases.claim: In Hassan, rains conventionally start in the 1st week of May and the monsoon sets in during the 1st week of June.
cases.expectedExcerpt: (Conventional rains actually start in 1 st week of May; Through Monsoon sets in 1 st week of June

cases.claim: The plan lists continuous high rainfall causing waterlogging as a contingency (crops listed are field crops; ginger is not named).
cases.expectedExcerpt: Continuous high rainfall in a short span leading to water logging
cases.notes: Ginger-specific contingency measures: none found in the document.
